subject: how much can we precompile?  + privacy

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: how much can we precompile?  + privacy
parts:
Topic I
-------

One issue that would be nice to address in this
refactoring is the time it takes to compile user models.

One thing we could do to speed this up is more
agressively precompile our libs.

The most general way to do this is to follow the
pattern set up in the grammars (which was forced
upon us by Windows compiler lameness).

The general idea is for each function foo()
would be to have three separate files:

foo.hpp pure header file, included by clients
who link against the precompile lib

foo_def.hpp actual definitions, included by
clients who want to use Stan as
a header only lib

foo_inst.cpp instantiations of the function's templates,
compiled into an archive for users to link
against; includes foo_def.hpp

Right now, the boundary between what gets separated
into .hpp and .cpp files seems rather arbitrary.

And yes, Daniel and I decided each function should go in
its own file a la Boost. It makes it much easier to
limit the scope of dependent includes and also makes the
code files and test files much easier to browse. They
were getting out of hand.

Topic II
--------

The other issue I do want to tackle is privatization.
We're exposing way too many of the internals of our lib
in the API.

What we want to expose is essentially the functions we
want to doc. The dividing line for me is in terms of
what functions a client (someone using the Stan C++ library)
might need.

Once we refactor, I'll do a much more thorough job of
doc on the C++ side. This makes it much easier for a new
developer to jump into the code and also makes it possible
for external clients to use Stan C++ as a library in their
own code.

Daniel's and my focus in doing this has been on the math
and probability libraries for a start, including the
auto-diff. We think that's the most likely piece of the
whole puzzle to be used as a library. Next most likely would
be the MCMC and sampling libs and also the model compiler.

Michael's working on refactoring the MCMC lib.

- Bob

P.S. When the dust settles, I think we'll have Stan 2.0.

P.P.S. After we fill out the forward-mode auto-diff lib
and get RM-HMC in, that can be Stan 3.0. I do not want
to be forever stuck at 1.x.y versions!
